## Comparability caveat

Alaska Air Group's FY2024 results are **not** directly comparable to its FY2022/FY2023 results: Alaska completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and Hawaiian's results are consolidated only from that date forward [DOC-2]. Alaska's 10-K discloses that Hawaiian contributed $869 million of revenue from the acquisition date through December 31, 2024 [DOC-2]. I therefore subtract that $869M from Alaska's FY2024 revenue of $11,735M [DOC-1] to get an ex-acquisition FY2024 base of $10,866M. Note this is an approximation of "organic" growth — it removes only the stub-period revenue of the acquired entity and does not adjust for any revenue synergies, network changes, or intercompany effects. The other four carriers are all calendar-year filers with no acquisition adjustment noted [DOC-1].

## FY2023 → FY2024 growth

| Rank | Airline | FY2023 | FY2024 (adj.) | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | United | $53,717M | $57,063M | +6.23% |
| 2 | Delta | $58,048M | $61,643M | +6.19% |
| 3 | Southwest | $26,091M | $27,483M | +5.34% |
| 4 | Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) | $10,426M | $10,866M | +4.22% |
| 5 | American | $52,788M | $54,211M | +2.70% |

United: $53,717M → $57,063M [DOC-1]. Delta: $58,048M → $61,643M [DOC-1]. Southwest: $26,091M → $27,483M [DOC-1]. American: $52,788M → $54,211M [DOC-1]. Alaska: $10,426M → $11,735M reported [DOC-1], less $869M Hawaiian revenue [DOC-2] = $10,866M. (Alaska's *reported* growth would be +12.56%, i.e. first place — the ranking change is entirely acquisition-driven.)

United's lead over Delta here is only ~4 basis points, so the top spot in this ranking is effectively a tie within rounding.

## FY2022 → FY2024 growth

| Rank | Airline | FY2022 | FY2024 (adj.) | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | United | $44,955M | $57,063M | +26.93% |
| 2 | Delta | $50,582M | $61,643M | +21.87% |
| 3 | Southwest | $23,814M | $27,483M | +15.41% |
| 4 | Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) | $9,646M | $10,866M | +12.65% |
| 5 | American | $48,971M | $54,211M | +10.70% |

United: $44,955M → $57,063M [DOC-1]. Delta: $50,582M → $61,643M [DOC-1]. Southwest: $23,814M → $27,483M [DOC-1]. American: $48,971M → $54,211M [DOC-1]. Alaska: $9,646M [DOC-1] → $10,866M (ex-Hawaiian) [DOC-1][DOC-2].

## Conclusion

Yes — **United Airlines Holdings ranks first in both periods**, though its FY23→FY24 lead over Delta is negligible (6.23% vs. 6.19%), while its two-year lead is decisive (26.9% vs. 21.9%). The ordering of the remaining four carriers is identical in both periods: Delta, Southwest, Alaska (ex-Hawaiian), American.

ANSWER: Yes — United is top-ranked in both. FY23→FY24 (ex-acquisition): United +6.23%, Delta +6.19%, Southwest +5.34%, Alaska +4.22%, American +2.70%. FY22→FY24: United +26.93%, Delta +21.87%, Southwest +15.41%, Alaska +12.65%, American +10.70%. (Alaska adjusted to exclude the $869M of Hawaiian revenue consolidated from Sept 18, 2024; on a reported basis Alaska would lead the FY23→FY24 ranking at +12.56%.)
